# An explicit nearly antipodal critical-pair exclusion in every d>=2

This is a local geometric criterion for an actual three-fiber critical
configuration. It does not assert that an arbitrary large enclosing
simplex forces such a pair of normals in dimensions greater than two.

## 1. Actual cap configuration and a quantitative two-cap criterion

Let d>=2, Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, and let omega_(d-1) be the ordinary
(d-1)-volume of the Euclidean unit ball in R^(d-1). Let A,K,B be
the only nonempty integer fibers, at bases -1,0,1 respectively, and
let them be full-dimensional convex bodies with (A+B)/2 subset K and masses
a,k,b. Let y be interior to K. Suppose two genuine depth-critical
ambient halfspaces through (0,y), each of total mass Q, have unit
continuous normals u,v and zero B-volume. Assume the two B cutting
planes are actual supporting planes, so their thresholds are
h_B(u),h_B(v). Suppose additionally

    r B_d subset B,     r>0,
    b<=a+k.

Define

    L=d 2^d k/[omega_(d-1) r^(d-1)],
    delta=|u+v|.

If

    delta L<=2r,
    omega_(d-1) delta L^d < (1-2Gamma)b,             (1)

then

    Q>Gamma(a+k+b)/2.                              (2)

The right side of the second inequality in (1) is positive because
d>=2 and Gamma<1/2.

**Proof.** Fix p in A. Compatibility puts the ball of radius r/2
centered at p/2 inside K. For any x in K, take the (d-1)-ball of
radius r/2 centered at p/2 in the perpendicular hyperplane to
x-p/2. Its convex hull with x is inside K and has d-volume

    [omega_(d-1)(r/2)^(d-1)/d] |x-p/2|.

Consequently |x-p/2|<=L/2. Applying this first to y and then to
arbitrary x, and allowing p to vary, gives

    K-y subset L B_d,
    2y-A subset L B_d.                             (3)

The two A traces are

    u.x>=2u.y-h_B(u),
    v.x>=2v.y-h_B(v).

Writing c=2y-x for x in A, a point missing both would satisfy
(u+v).c>h_B(u)+h_B(v)>=2r. This contradicts (3) and delta L<=2r.
Thus the two A captures cover A exactly.

A point z=x-y of the middle fiber missing both traces has u.z<0
and v.z<0. Since v=-u+(u+v), this implies
-delta L<u.z<0. The missed middle mass therefore lies in a strip
of width delta L in a ball of radius L. Its volume is at most

    E=omega_(d-1) delta L^d.                        (4)

Sum the actual masses of the two critical halfspaces: their B masses
are zero, their A traces cover A, and their K traces miss at most E.
Hence a+k<=2Q+E. If Q<=Gamma(a+k+b)/2, then

    Q<=Gamma(a+k),
    E>=a+k-2Q>=(1-2Gamma)(a+k)>=(1-2Gamma)b,

contradicting (1). This proves (2). All nonzero-continuous-normal
boundary sections have zero d-volume, so closed caps are retained
without a limiting argument. QED.

## 2. A dimension-only angular threshold in an actual normalized circuit

Suppose now that d+1 ambient caps through the actual source all attain
Q, all their A cuts are proper, all their B captures have zero volume,
and their continuous normals form a full-rank minimal positive circuit.
Assume B is nonheavy, b<=a+k; no global depth-maximizer hypothesis is
needed. Apply one
continuous affine map identically to all fibers, chosen by sending a
maximum-volume inscribed simplex of B to conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), and
then translating its centroid to zero. In this coordinate system

    r B_d subset B,       r=1/[(d+1)sqrt(d)],
    1/d!<=b<=2^d.                                  (5)

The maximum-volume simplex exists by compactness. Replacing its i-th
vertex by a point of B shows that every barycentric coordinate of that
point has absolute value at most one. Thus before recentering,
B subset [-1,1]^d, which proves the upper volume bound. The displayed
r is the distance from the standard simplex centroid to its nearest
facet, which is the facet sum x_i=1. This proves (5) without invoking
an unquantified normalization theorem.

Put

    C_d=3d 2^d/[omega_(d-1) r^(d-1)],

    epsilon_d=min{
        r/(C_d 2^d),
        (1-2Gamma)/[2 omega_(d-1) C_d^d 2^(d(d-1))]
    } >0.                                         (6)

Normalize the transformed continuous normals to unit length. If any
two satisfy

    |u_i+u_j|<=epsilon_d,                           (7)

then the source has Q>Gamma(a+k+b)/2.

**Proof.** First genuine criticality and proper A cuts force every
zero B cut to be an actual supporting plane: otherwise its B threshold
can be moved slightly toward B while the unchanged middle trace and
the decreased proper A cap yield a smaller total. The positive circuit
implies that the middle traces cover the whole space, and the A traces
also cover it. Indeed for positive dependence coefficients alpha_i,
sum alpha_i h_B(u_i)>0, whereas the weighted sum of their A thresholds
2u_i.y-h_B(u_i) is negative.

We record the required bad-target mass bound explicitly. Let U_i be the
A cap volumes, sorted increasingly, and put w=max U_i. Varying only
the integer coefficient of a cap with A mass w equalizes its endpoint
masses at t,t. Actual Brunn--Minkowski (or the trivial t=0 case)
gives t<=Q-w; genuine criticality gives w<=2t. Thus w<=2Q/3.

For Gamma<=1/2 and Gamma>1/3 put kappa=1/Gamma-2 in [0,1). The
ordinary positive-part cap-cover inequality, applied at the third
largest cap volume, gives

    a<=U_(d+1)+U_d+kappa U_(d-1),
    k<=Q/Gamma-U_1-U_2-kappa U_3.

This also applies when indices overlap at d=2: the displayed sums
are ordinary real sums, and all U_i are nonnegative. Bound the three
positive terms by (2+kappa)w=w/Gamma and discard the negative terms.
It follows that

    a+k<=Q/Gamma+w/Gamma<=5Q/(3Gamma).              (8)

The positive-part inequality used here follows by successively trimming
parallel caps to a common retained volume and applying ordinary
Grünbaum to the retained convex body. Its complete all-dimensional
proof and these exact three-term formulas appear in Sections 3--4 of
`candidate eb88c1c4c388daab`;
those profile steps do not require a simplex middle fiber.

Assume Q<=Gamma(a+k+b)/2. Equation (8) gives

    2Q/Gamma<=b+5Q/(3Gamma),
    Q<=3Gamma b,
    k<=3b.                                        (9)

The last inequality follows from the middle profile k<=Q/Gamma
minus nonnegative U terms, not from any global-maximizer premise.

Therefore the radius in Section 1 satisfies L<=C_d b. Using (5)--(7),

    delta L<=epsilon_d C_d 2^d<=r<2r,
    omega_(d-1)delta L^d/b
       <=omega_(d-1)epsilon_d C_d^d 2^(d(d-1))
       <=(1-2Gamma)/2 <1-2Gamma.

Both conditions (1) hold, contradicting the assumed bad target. QED.

If B is heavy instead, its ordinary centroid is an actual point with
raw mixed depth at least Gamma b>Gamma(a+k+b)/2. This proves existence
of a suitable actual point in that case, without claiming that the
original source has the same guarantee.

## Scope

Every constant in (6) is explicit in d and ordinary unit-ball volume.
The criterion is imposed in the specified maximum-inscribed-simplex
coordinate frame; no affine-invariance of Euclidean angles is assumed.
The normalization preserves the integer coordinate, all ambient
halfspaces, and all normalized mixed masses. Its transformed unit
normals, not the original normals, occur in (7).

In the plane, a large three-support triangle forces such an almost
opposite pair with an explicit estimate, giving the stronger numerical
threshold in
`candidate 2bb708ddf25004e0`.
No corresponding implication from a large support simplex is asserted
here for higher dimension. The result remains a conditional critical-cap
criterion, not a general OC theorem.
